newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's industrial slump to continue - poll.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's industrial slump to continue - poll.

text.p: The economic slump that has cut into industrial output across Colombia so far this year is not expected to end any time soon, a closely-watched survey of national business conditions said Wednesday.

An overwhelming 86.1 percent of participants in the survey by the National Association of Industrialists (ANDI) said they expect business conditions to either remain the same or worsen in the near-term.

According to the survey -- based on responses from industrialists across Colombia -- industrial production fell by 1.3 percent during the first nine months of the year to its lowest level in the past decade.
Industrial sales, which dropped 2.5 percent, also reached an historic low and 78 percent of those responding rated current business conditions as fair to poor.
In a summary of the survey's results, ANDI quoted most industrialists interviewed as saying they were very concerned by the continuing deterioration in the business climate.
Flagging demand was seen as the leading obstacle to growth in business and industrial activity, cited by 31.3 percent of participants in the ANDI survey.

Unlike previous surveys, it made no mention of political instability or the security threat posed by leftist guerrilla activity. But it said many industries had also been adversely affected by high financial costs and problems collecting payments.

Colombia's slowdown so far this year has been blamed by the government -- which says economic growth should still reach about 3.5 percent this year -- on mostly cyclical factors and growing trade in contraband goods entering the country.
